pattern.top_pattern: GA inpatient growth is concentrated in infection, sepsis, cellulitis, and femur fracture cases
key_driver_codes: DSPL IT FX LT FEMUR INITIAL CLOS FX
Hip and Femur Procedures Except Major Joint with CC
Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
pattern.pattern_details: GA clinical pressure is not broad-based. It is concentrated in a small set of infection, sepsis, cellulitis, and femur fracture presentations that are driving inpatient use and, in some cases, higher paid per admit. This clinical concentration helps explain why GA authorized acute hospital costs are rising and gives UM and clinical teams a focused set of pathways to review.
pattern.why_it_matters: Targeted clinical management is more likely to reduce avoidable inpatient use here than broad policy changes.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Have clinical and UM teams review admission appropriateness, observation versus inpatient use, and discharge planning for GA UTI, sepsis, cellulitis, and femur fracture episodes.
evidence_summary: UTI site not specified adds about $245K with 30 more admissions in kidney and urinary infection stays.
Sepsis unspecified organism adds about $196K with 21 more admissions.
Cellulitis of the left lower limb adds about $119K with 12 more admissions and about $2.7K higher paid per admit.
Left femur fracture adds about $198K with 15 more admissions.
